```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kovanda_2017_isavuconazole"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kovanda_2017_isavuconazole"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.00101-17> (open access, PMC5444187)

Kovanda 2017 asked whether mucositis reduces the oral absorption of
isavuconazole. Patients from the phase 3 SECURE and VITAL trials who took the
oral prodrug (isavuconazonium sulfate 372 mg, equivalent to 200 mg
isavuconazole) were split by whether the oral dosing and the plasma samples
coincided with an episode of mucositis. A nonparametric population PK model
was fitted in Pmetrics, with mucositis switching the oral bioavailability
between two estimated values:

`F = F1 x (1 - MUC) + F12 x MUC`

The median bioavailability was 99.8% without and 98.3% with mucositis, and the
average daily exposure (AUCave) did not differ between the groups. All doses
in this article are expressed as isavuconazole.

# Population

A total of 250 patients were included: 56 with mucositis and 194 without (Kovanda
2017 Table 1). Median age was 52 years (range 18-92), mean weight 70.0 +/-
18.3 kg, 62% were male, and 79% were White, 15% Asian, 4% Black and 2% other.
Mucositis patients were mostly haematological-malignancy patients (89.3%),
78.2% were neutropenic at baseline and 26.8% had received an allogeneic HSCT.
The loading regimen was 200 mg every 8 h for 48 h (i.v. in SECURE, i.v. or
oral in VITAL), then 200 mg once daily i.v. or oral. Median total duration was
75.5 days with and 83 days without mucositis. The median i.v. duration was 9
and 7 days respectively (Table 1). Trough samples were taken on days 7, 14 and
42 and at the end of therapy, with full 24-h profiles in 43 patients.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kovanda_2017_isavuconazole"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Structure: gut compartment with lag, Ka and F into a central compartment, i.v. infusion into central, CL/V elimination | n/a | Figure 3; Results, 'Population PK (PPK) model' |
| `F = F1 x (1 - MUC) + F12 x MUC` | n/a | Methods, 'PPK modeling' |
| `lka` | log(7.9 1/h) | Table 2, Ka, nonmucositis median |
| `lcl` | log(1.9 L/h) | Table 2, CL/F, nonmucositis median |
| `lvc` | log(349.8 L) | Table 2, V/F, nonmucositis median |
| `ltlag` | log(1.0 h) | Table 2, lag time, nonmucositis median |
| `lfdepot` (F1) | log(0.998) | Table 2, F, nonmucositis median; Abstract |
| `e_dis_mucositis_fdepot` | -0.01503 | Derived: F12 / F1 - 1 = 0.983 / 0.998 - 1; Table 2, F, mucositis median; Abstract |
| `etalka` | 0.191942 | Table 2, Ka CV 46% (nonmucositis), log(CV^2 + 1) |
| `etalcl` | 0.199588 | Table 2, CL/F CV 47% (nonmucositis), log(CV^2 + 1) |
| `etalvc` | 0.239332 | Table 2, V/F CV 52% (nonmucositis), log(CV^2 + 1) |
| `etaltlag` | 0.723143 | Table 2, lag time CV 103% (nonmucositis), log(CV^2 + 1) |
| `propSd` | fixed(0) | Not reported (Methods: weighting by the inverse of the estimated assay variance; no coefficients printed) |

# Regimen and virtual cohort

The simulated regimen follows the trial protocols and the Table 1 medians for
each group. The 200 mg every 8 h loading doses are given i.v. for 48 h, then
200 mg once daily i.v. up to the group's median i.v. duration, then 200 mg
once daily orally to the group's median total duration. I.v. doses are 1-h
infusions into `central`, and oral doses go to `depot`.

```{r regimen}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,     ~DIS_MUCOSITIS, ~iv_days, ~total_days, ~aucave_median,
  "Nonmucositis", 0,              7,        83,          100.2,
  "Mucositis",    1,              9,        75.5,        91.9
)

make_events <- function(ids, treatment, muc, iv_days, total_days, grid_h) {
  end_h <- total_days * 24
  dose <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = seq(0, 40, by = 8), cmt = "central", rate = 200),
    data.frame(time = seq(48, (iv_days - 1) * 24, by = 24), cmt = "central", rate = 200),
    data.frame(time = seq(iv_days * 24, end_h - 1, by = 24), cmt = "depot", rate = 0)
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 200, evid = 1L)
  obs <- data.frame(
    time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, end_h, by = grid_h), 14 * 24, 42 * 24))),
    cmt = "central", rate = NA_real_, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L
  )
  one <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs)
  tidyr::crossing(id = ids, one) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      treatment = treatment, DIS_MUCOSITIS = muc, end_h = end_h
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

build_events <- function(n_per_arm, grid_h) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
    r <- regimens[i, ]
    make_events(
      ids = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm),
      treatment = r$treatment, muc = r$DIS_MUCOSITIS,
      iv_days = r$iv_days, total_days = r$total_days, grid_h = grid_h
    )
  }))
}

events_typ <- build_events(n_per_arm = 1L, grid_h = 1)
events <- build_events(n_per_arm = 200L, grid_h = 2)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Kovanda_2017_isavuconazole")
keep_cols <- c("treatment", "DIS_MUCOSITIS", "end_h")

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = events_typ, keep = keep_cols,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170517)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = events, keep = keep_cols, returnType = "data.frame"
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc), !anyNA(sim_typ$Cc))
```

## Mucositis acts on oral bioavailability only

With every dose given orally, the typical-value AUC ratio between the two arms
must equal `F12 / F1` exactly, because clearance, volume, Ka and the lag time
are shared. This checks that the covariate reaches only `f(depot)`.

```{r f-ratio}
oral_only <- tidyr::crossing(
  id = 1:2,
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = seq(0, 24 * 29, by = 24), amt = 200, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(time = seq(0, 24 * 30, by = 0.25), amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "depot")
  )
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(DIS_MUCOSITIS = id - 1L) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
s_oral <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = oral_only,
                          returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
auc_oral <- s_oral |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2))
ratio <- auc_oral$auc[2] / auc_oral$auc[1]
ratio
# Deterministic identity: the two solves differ only in F.
stopifnot(abs(ratio / (0.983 / 0.998) - 1) < 1e-6)
```

# Average daily exposure (AUCave)

Kovanda 2017 computed each patient's AUCave by integrating their Bayesian
posterior profile over the whole dosing period and dividing by the number of
days of therapy (Methods). The unit is mg.h/L per day. AUCave is 24 times the
average concentration over the dosing period, so PKNCA's `cav` over
`[0, end of therapy]` gives it directly.

## Typical value

AUCave is close to `F x Dose / CL` per day, which is monotone in CL. The
median of the individual AUCave values therefore maps onto the median CL, and
the typical-value AUCave is a fair estimate of the published group medians.

```{r aucave-typical}
aucave_typ <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, end_h) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(aucave = auc / (end_h / 24)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(regimens |> dplyr::select(treatment, aucave_median),
                   by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (aucave / aucave_median - 1))

aucave_typ |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, aucave, aucave_median, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = treatment,
    "Typical-value AUCave (mg.h/L)" = aucave,
    "Published median AUCave (mg.h/L)" = aucave_median,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value AUCave against the Table 2 medians.")

pct <- setNames(aucave_typ$pct_diff, aucave_typ$treatment)
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic: a mis-transcribed CL, F, dose or unit moves this by tens
  # of percent. Realised +0.6%.
  abs(pct[["Nonmucositis"]]) < 5,
  # Deterministic. Realised +7.9%: the mucositis F distribution is strongly
  # left-skewed (mean 86.0% vs median 98.3%), which pulls the median of
  # F x Dose / CL below the typical-value prediction. See the deviations.
  abs(pct[["Mucositis"]]) < 10
)
```

## Stochastic cohort with PKNCA

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- regimens |>
  dplyr::transmute(treatment, start = 0, end = total_days * 24, cav = TRUE)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

# Published Table 2 median AUCave (mg.h/L per day) expressed as the average
# concentration over the dosing period: cav = AUCave / 24.
published <- regimens |>
  dplyr::transmute(treatment, cav = aucave_median / 24)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cav = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (cohort median, 200 per arm) vs. published median average",
    "concentration over the dosing period (AUCave / 24). * differs by >20%."
  )
)
```

```{r pknca-gate}
cav_sim <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  dplyr::mutate(aucave = PPORRES * 24)
cohort_pct <- cav_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(aucave_median_sim = median(aucave), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(regimens |> dplyr::select(treatment, aucave_median),
                   by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (aucave_median_sim / aucave_median - 1))
cohort_pct
cp <- setNames(cohort_pct$pct_diff, cohort_pct$treatment)
stopifnot(
  # Cohort medians of 200 subjects: Monte Carlo SE of the median is about
  # 1.25 x 0.45 / sqrt(200) = 4% on the log scale, so these bounds sit more
  # than 3 SE from the typical-value differences (+0.6% and +7.9%) and
  # still fail on a mis-transcribed CL, F, dose or unit.
  abs(cp[["Nonmucositis"]]) < 15,
  abs(cp[["Mucositis"]]) < 22
)
```

## Figure 6: AUCave by group

```{r figure-6}
fig6_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,     ~q25, ~q50,  ~q75,
  "Mucositis",    58,   91.9,  128,
  "Nonmucositis", 71,   100.2, 125
)
cav_sim |>
  ggplot(aes(treatment, aucave)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(data = fig6_pub, aes(treatment, q50), colour = "red",
             shape = 4, size = 4, stroke = 1.5) +
  geom_errorbar(data = fig6_pub, aes(x = treatment, ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "red", width = 0.15) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 400)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "AUCave (mg.h/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 6 of Kovanda 2017. Boxes: simulated cohort (200 per arm).",
      "Red: published median (Table 2) and interquartile range digitised from Figure 6."
    )
  )
```

## Figure 2: trough concentrations during oral therapy

Figure 2 pools the observed plasma concentrations drawn during oral dosing
after day 7. The simulated equivalent below takes the day-14 and day-42
troughs, which fall 24 h after an oral dose in both arms.

```{r figure-2}
troughs <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(14 * 24, 42 * 24))
fig2_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,     ~q25, ~q50, ~q75,
  "Nonmucositis", 2.65, 3.9,  5.2,
  "Mucositis",    2.1,  2.95, 3.95
)
trough_sum <- troughs |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q25_sim = quantile(Cc, 0.25), q50_sim = median(Cc), q75_sim = quantile(Cc, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig2_pub, by = "treatment")
trough_sum |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = treatment,
    "Simulated Q1 (mg/L)" = q25_sim, "Simulated median (mg/L)" = q50_sim,
    "Simulated Q3 (mg/L)" = q75_sim, "Figure 2 Q1 (mg/L)" = q25,
    "Figure 2 median (mg/L)" = q50, "Figure 2 Q3 (mg/L)" = q75
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Trough concentrations, simulated vs. digitised Figure 2.")

troughs |>
  ggplot(aes(treatment, Cc)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(data = fig2_pub, aes(treatment, q50), colour = "red",
             shape = 4, size = 4, stroke = 1.5) +
  geom_errorbar(data = fig2_pub, aes(x = treatment, ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "red", width = 0.15) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 15)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Isavuconazole trough (mg/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 2 of Kovanda 2017. Boxes: simulated day-14 and day-42 troughs.",
      "Red: median and interquartile range digitised from Figure 2."
    )
  )

tr <- setNames(trough_sum$q50_sim / trough_sum$q50 - 1, trough_sum$treatment)
# Nonmucositis only; the mucositis trough is a recorded deviation (below).
stopifnot(abs(tr[["Nonmucositis"]]) < 0.2)
```

## Concentration-time profile

```{r profile}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 21 * 24) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Isavuconazole Cc (mg/L)",
    caption = "Median and 90% prediction interval over the first 3 weeks of the simulated regimen."
  )
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Typical values are the Table 2 medians.** Table 2 is titled 'Median
  parameter estimates' and the Abstract quotes the median bioavailabilities
  (98.3% and 99.8%). The shared parameters (Ka, CL, V, lag time) use the
  nonmucositis column, which is the `MUC = 0` reference. The mucositis-column
  medians are identical for Ka, CL and the lag time, and 0.6% lower for V
  (347.7 vs 349.8 L).
- **F12 is re-expressed as a fractional effect.** The paper estimates F12
  directly. The model writes `F = F1 x (1 + e x DIS_MUCOSITIS)` with
  `e = 0.983 / 0.998 - 1 = -0.01503`, which is the same function.
- **Systemic, not apparent, CL and V.** Table 2 labels them 'CL/F' and 'V/F',
  but Figure 3 routes i.v. infusions directly into the central compartment
  and F is the absolute oral bioavailability. So CL and V are systemic, and F
  applies to oral doses only.
- **Interindividual variability is a parametric approximation.** Pmetrics
  estimates a discrete nonparametric density. The Table 2 CV% values of the
  nonmucositis group are encoded as independent lognormal marginals
  (`omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`), as in the other Pmetrics models in this
  library. The mucositis group's CVs are somewhat lower (Ka 38%, CL 44%, V 47%,
  lag time 94%). Two marginals fit poorly:
  - Ka has its median (7.9 1/h) at the top of its 0-8 1/h range with the mean
    (6.5) below it. The distribution is left-skewed, and a lognormal cannot
    match both summaries. The trough-dominated data carry little information
    on Ka, and AUC does not depend on it.
  - F has no IIV. Both medians sit within 2% of 1, so a lognormal marginal is
    physically impossible and a logit-normal one is not identified from a
    CV. The mucositis F distribution is strongly left-skewed (mean 86.0%, range
    50.3-99.7%), and this spread is not reproduced.
- **Residual error is not reported.** The Methods state only that the data
  were weighted by the inverse of the estimated assay variance. The
  assay-error polynomial and any gamma or lambda are not printed, so `propSd`
  is fixed at zero.
- **Infusion duration.** The paper does not state it. The simulations use a
  1-h infusion, the minimum infusion time in the isavuconazonium sulfate
  label. The model takes the rate from the event record, and AUCave barely
  depends on it.
- **Regimen.** Patients switched between i.v. and oral at the investigator's
  discretion. The simulated regimen is one representative schedule per group
  built from the Table 1 medians (i.v. 7 or 9 days, total 83 or 75.5 days).
  The published AUCave values summarise each patient's own regimen.
- **Mucositis-group AUCave and troughs.** The typical-value AUCave
  reproduces the nonmucositis median to +0.6%, and the mucositis median to
  +7.9%. The typical-value day-14 troughs of the two arms differ by only 1%
  (3.88 and 3.85 mg/L), and the simulated nonmucositis troughs match the
  digitised Figure 2 median and interquartile range. The digitised Figure 2
  median for mucositis patients, however, is about 2.95 mg/L, some 25% lower.
  The paper reports this raw-trough difference as statistically significant
  (P = 0.0011) and does not attribute it to any model parameter. The median
  F12 is only 1.5% below F1 and no other parameter carries a mucositis effect,
  so the packaged model cannot reproduce it. The left tail of the individual
  F12 posteriors (mean 86.0%, which a model without IIV on F does not carry)
  would explain about half of it at most. The difference is recorded here and
  not gated.
- **Digitised values.** The Figure 2 medians and interquartile ranges, and the
  Figure 6 interquartile ranges, were digitised by the maintainers from the
  published figures to about +/-0.1 mg/L and +/-3 mg.h/L respectively. The
  Figure 6 medians are the Table 2 values.
- **No correction notice** was found for this article (Crossref, checked
  2026-11-25).
